Subject: MSA redline: third-party IP coverage and evidence timing

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking our MSA redline. Two items legal flagged during procurement review that we wanted to surface early so we can align before the signature window:

1) Defense control for third-party IP claims — our standard is that the vendor (you) takes defense but we require the ability to step in if vendor declines or there is a material conflict. We redlined for a defend-vs-reimburse structure (vendor defends; customer can take over if vendor refuses) with a 30-day cure.

2) Evidence / remediation timing — procurement wants clearer SLAs for evidence preservation and an evidence checklist so our security/compliance team can validate quickly.

I attached the redline and a procurement checklist. Can you confirm Redwood's stance on defend vs reimburse and whether you can provide an evidence checklist and an estimated review turnaround? We are hoping to finalize commercial terms by 12/15.

Best,
Sonia

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-12-01T15:50:00-08:00
Subject: RE: MSA redline: third-party IP coverage and evidence timing (internal counsel)

Ben / Lauren — I reviewed TerrainBio's redline. Below are legal's recommended positions and a suggested middle ground that should be acceptable to procurement. High-level: we prefer to retain defense control for third-party IP (better for consistency and managing litigation risk), but we can offer a limited hybrid that addresses TerrainBio's concern about conflicts and time-to-remedy.

Suggested compromise (tracked language snippet):
"If a third party asserts a claim that the Customer's use of the Services infringes or misappropriates a third party's intellectual property rights, Redwood will, at its option, either (a) assume and control the defense of such claim, including the selection of counsel; or (b) if Redwood reasonably determines that a conflict exists or Redwood is unable to defend, Redwood will promptly notify Customer and reimburse Customer for reasonable defense costs incurred after Customer assumes control, subject to the insurance offset and mutual cooperation provisions below. Customer must notify Redwood in writing within 30 days of receipt of notice of claim and provide the evidence set forth in Schedule X. Redwood will not be liable for any settlement made without Redwood's prior written consent (which will not be unreasonably withheld)."

Key points to include in Schedule X (evidence checklist):
- Date/time of alleged incident
- Copy of complaint/notice from third party
- Any output examples (prompt + model output) linked to the allegedly infringing result
- System logs showing request IDs and KV cache snapshots if available
- Customer statements about remedial steps taken

Insurance/offset mechanics: propose a simple waterfall: first use any applicable vendor liability insurance, then reduce Redwood's cash obligation by the insurance recovery amount (we can document the calculation in the order form). That addresses procurement's insurance posture without creating an open-ended obligation.

Cap suggestion: for this commercial stage, recommend a defense cap at $3,000,000 aggregate for third-party IP claims (can be discussed as part of discount/credit tradeoffs). If procurement pushes back, we can table the cap and offer higher service credits / extended support SLA in lieu.

I can draft a tracked redline of the MSA + a Schedule X evidence checklist. Setting team ask for Ben: propose two options to the customer (Option A: Redwood defends up to $3M; Option B: customer defends and Redwood reimburses up to $1.5M net of insurance). That way procurement can choose a path aligned with their risk appetite.

Attachments: I will attach a draft Schedule X and a short note on the insurance offset calc.

Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@terrainbio.com>
Cc: legal@terrainbio.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-12-02T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: two-path compromise on third-party IP defense (options attached)

Sonia — thanks again for the quick turnaround. Kimberly and I discussed and we can offer two commercially viable options; we want to be transparent so your procurement and legal can pick the path that fits TerrainBio's risk model. See both options below and attached tracked redline + evidence checklist.

Option A (Preferred) — Redwood-led defense
- Redwood will assume control of defense of third-party IP claims and manage counsel selection.
- Aggregate liability cap: $3,000,000 for third-party IP claims (negotiable).
- Insurance offset: Redwood's payment obligations are reduced by insurance recoveries reasonably attributable to the claim.
- Schedule X evidence list to enable quick triage (attached).

Option B — Customer-led defense with reimbursement
- Customer may assume defense if Redwood elects not to or if a conflict exists. Redwood will reimburse reasonable defense costs up to $1,500,000 net of any insurance recoveries.
- Cooperation clause & standard notice windows apply.

Next steps: can you confirm which option TerrainBio prefers by COB 2028-12-08? If neither works, we can set a short call with Kimberly to walk Procurement through the insurance/off-set calculation and the evidence requirements.

Attachments: TerrainBio_MSA_redline_20281203.pdf (tracked MSA with our proposed language), rdw-evidence-checklist-template.xlsx

Appreciate it —
Ben
From: Adam Ruiz <adam.ruiz@terrainbio.com>

Subject: Re: Proposal: two-path compromise on third-party IP defense (options attached)

Ben — thanks for the quick options. A few initial responses from our counsel:

- We prefer Option B (Customer-led defense with reimbursement) but need the cap increased — $3M is too low for us in this space given potential downstream commercial exposure. We would consider $5M or an unlimited carve subject to insurance recoveries.
- Procurement needs clearer evidence-handling SLAs (for example, log retention windows; a contact for real-time evidence pulls).
- We appreciate Redwood's suggested Schedule X. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide automated log extracts for a rolling 90-day window on request? That would materially reduce the friction for our engineering team.

Finally, we have a procurement timing constraint: our board reviews commercial terms on 12/12. If we can't reach an agreement on defense/limit mechanics before then, we risk pushing signature into January. Can Kimberly join a 30-min call on 12/05 at 10am PT?

Regards,
Adam Ruiz
Senior Counsel, TerrainBio

Kim / Lauren — TerrainBio responded and prefers Option B but is pushing for a $5M cap and improved evidence access. Board review is 12/12; they asked for a call 12/05 at 10am PT with Kimberly present.

Recommended negotiation posture:
- Push back on an uncapped exposure. Offer to increase the reimbursement cap to $3M with an option to expand to $5M tied to a commercial concession (e.g., a 6-month committed usage discount or a higher order-form commitment).
- Confirm our ability to provide automated 90-day log extracts for triage purposes (ops to confirm technical feasibility; cc'd Sam).
- Prepare a tracked redline that shows the $3M/$5M trade and a short paragraph on insurance offset mechanics. If TerrainBio needs $5M, we should ask for an elevated commercial concession or longer-term commitment.

Action items:
1) Kim — please join the 12/05 call and prepare the tracked redline with the two-tier cap proposal and a one-paragraph negotiation script.
2) Sam — can you confirm by EOD whether automated 90-day log exports are available on request and any limitations (format, latency)?
3) Lauren — FYI for potential credit/discount structuring if the cap increases.

I’ll set the invite for 12/05 10am PT once Kim confirms availability.

Thanks,
